title: Providers: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, DigitalOcean, Hetzner and Linode

videos.script: You are about to choose where your software will live, or to join a team that already chose. The names arrive fast. AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, and then a group that looks smaller: DigitalOcean, Hetzner and Linode. {{names}} This lesson is a map of that market. It will not tell you who is biggest this quarter, because that number is stale before a lesson ships. It tells you what kind of company each one is, and what it is known for. {{kinds}} There are two kinds of provider. The big three sell hundreds of managed services, in regions all over the world. The smaller ones sell a short list and a simpler bill. Neither kind is a toy. {{catalogue}} Then you will learn to translate. A virtual machine is EC2 on AWS, Virtual Machines on Azure and Compute Engine on Google Cloud. Once you can translate, the rest of this course reads the same on any of them. {{table}} After that, you will read a real price list. AWS publishes its whole list as files anyone can download, and you will pull one machine's price for two regions out of it. {{prices}} The lesson ends with a checklist, not a winner. The right provider depends on what you build, where your users are, and what your team already knows. {{choose}}
